candidate.title: Recall, reconnect and try again

prompts: Without the worked example, explain: Retrieve and explain learning from the six accepted periods without opening worked support.
Without the worked example, explain: Choose a relevant misconception card and improve an explanation with guided evidence.

pedagogy.rationale: Independent retrieval precedes teacher-selected support and a fresh retry. Six period cards preserve all 23 named source misconceptions; selection is teacher-guided, not an automatic diagnosis.

prerequisiteAssumptions: Use work from lessons actually attempted today.
Read with teacher support or explain orally to a scribe as needed.

misconceptions.description: Copying a worked answer is taken as evidence of independent recall.
misconceptions.response: Try first without support, use the selected card to reconnect the idea, then answer a fresh question without copying.

misconceptions.description: A final answer is offered without the step, observation or text detail that supports it.
misconceptions.response: Identify the relevant step, observation or text detail and explain how it supports your answer.

scenes.title: Choose the card that helps your reasoning
scenes.learnerAction: Choose one relevant card, work with its guidance and explain which evidence supports the correction.

content.body: With your teacher, choose a card for an explanation you want to improve. You do not need every card. Use its model or evidence, then explain the correction in your own words. Keep your first attempt. Tokens are a model, not measurements of nutrients in a person.

prompts.prompt: Name the card you chose and explain your correction.

Better idea: Name the full place values before multiplying: 2 hundreds is 200, not 2. Reconnect: Represent 312 as 300, 10 and 2. Multiply each full value by 3 before combining. Card 2. Better idea: Keep the value of every partial product and regroup it into the correct place rather than deleting it. Reconnect: Trade ten ones for one ten without throwing away value. Show how 4 times 4 ones becomes one ten and six ones. P2: choose a relevant card with your teacher. Card 1. blocks.title: P2: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: The swallowed food route is drawn through the liver or pancreas instead of distinguishing the juices they supply. Better idea: Keep the continuous food route separate from the liver and pancreas, which supply digestive juices. Reconnect: Use one arrow for swallowed food and different arrows for digestive juices. Place liver and pancreas beside the food route.

Card 2. A mistake to check: The stomach is treated as the place where all nutrients enter the body. Better idea: Most digested nutrients are absorbed through the small-intestine wall. Reconnect: Compare the stomach with the small intestine. Locate where most digested nutrients enter the body.

Card 3. A mistake to check: Nutrients that cross the wall are treated as disappearing from the model total. Better idea: Keep transferred tokens visible in the body region. Count both regions to conserve the total. Reconnect: Move paper nutrient tokens into a body region while keeping every token visible. Transferred tokens still exist.

Card 4. A mistake to check: The starting count is reported as still inside after tokens have crossed the wall. Better idea: The starting count describes both regions together. Subtract transferred tokens to find what remains inside. Reconnect: Label the starting total before moving tokens. Label the tokens still in the first region separately.

Card 5. A mistake to check: The number transferred during a round is confused with the number remaining inside. Better idea: Transferred and remaining name different groups. Track the inside count after every transfer. Reconnect: Keep transferred and remaining tokens in two labelled groups. Point to the group named by each question.

blocks.title: P3: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: A plausible prediction is reported as something the story has already established. Better idea: Name the detail that makes the idea plausible, use might or may, and change the prediction if later evidence conflicts. Reconnect: Mark an early clue, your prediction and a later detail in the accepted reading text. Treat the prediction as a possibility.

Card 2. A mistake to check: A summary lists incidental details or invents an outcome instead of connecting the central problem, response and result. Better idea: Keep the problem, the action taken and the result supported by the story; remove details that do not explain that connection. Reconnect: Choose details that explain the main problem, response and result. Put minor details aside.

blocks.title: P4: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: Every inland location is assumed to be high or mountainous. Better idea: Inland means away from the coast. A broad terrain description does not determine every local elevation. Reconnect: Separate coastal or inland labels from evidence about elevation or a particular route. Use the accepted records.

Card 2. A mistake to check: One observation or place description is treated as evidence about all communities. Better idea: Name the place and observation, limit the conclusion to that evidence and seek additional observations. Reconnect: Compare what the two club records actually describe. One record does not describe every place.

Card 3. A mistake to check: Coastal or inland is treated as enough evidence to select a safe site. Better idea: Compare the actual site, path and local observations. A region label alone does not establish safety. Reconnect: Match each room or route claim to its actual observation. A place name does not establish safety.

Card 4. A mistake to check: General coast-to-inland landform descriptions are treated as exact county boundaries. Better idea: Use an administrative map for county boundaries. A physical sketch does not establish those lines. Reconnect: Use separate labels for a physical region and an administrative county. They answer different kinds of questions.

Card 5. A mistake to check: Evidence about a dry room or a clear path is treated as proving the other requirement too. Better idea: Check each requirement separately. Room and route observations answer different questions. Reconnect: Make separate columns for room conditions and route access. Check each need with relevant evidence.

blocks.title: P5: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: The variable's name is changed whenever its number changes. Better idea: Keep the name score fixed and replace the number stored beneath it. Reconnect: Keep the score name card fixed and replace only the number card when its value changes.

Card 2. A mistake to check: Set score to a number is treated as adding that number. Better idea: Set replaces the current value. Add uses the current value to calculate the next one. Reconnect: Compare set to 2 with add 2 from the same starting score of 4. Set replaces; add uses the previous value.

Card 3. A mistake to check: Initialization is repeated before every event, discarding the accumulated score. Better idea: Initialize at new-game start and retain the updated value between events. Reconnect: Initialize at the start of a new game. Keep the updated value between hits unless a reset event occurs.

Card 4. A mistake to check: A set instruction is ignored and the previous value is retained. Better idea: Follow every instruction in order. Set replaces the old value even if no points were earned. Reconnect: Follow every instruction in order, including set. Replace the number even when no points were earned.

Card 5. A mistake to check: A new game starts without initialization and inherits an earlier game's score. Better idea: Give each new game its stated starting value before processing events. Reconnect: Show the end of one game and the starting value of a new game on separate cards. Initialize the new game.

blocks.title: P6: choose a relevant card with your teacher
paragraphs: Card 1. A mistake to check: The switch creates the energy that lights the lamp. Better idea: The battery supplies energy. Closing the switch completes a conducting path; the switch does not create energy. Reconnect: Sketch the battery, lamp and conducting return path. Open and close the switch on the sketch.

Card 2. A mistake to check: One successful test proves the switch always works. Better idea: Record every trial, including failures. Five trials support a limited comparison, not a guarantee. Reconnect: Read every actual or explicitly supplied trial from the accepted Engineering activity. Include failures and identify the source.

Card 3. A mistake to check: Changing several components establishes which single change caused an outcome. Better idea: Change one contact feature while keeping battery, bulb, wires and procedure fixed. Reconnect: Name one contact feature to change. Keep battery, lamp, wires and procedure fixed.

Card 4. A mistake to check: The taller closed-switch bar proves the best design without checking open-switch control. Better idea: Use both closed-light and open-dark observations, and acknowledge the limits of the tests. Reconnect: Read both closed-light bars, then inspect both open-dark counts. Both criteria matter.
